Mean shape of a sample of 3D or 2D landmark configurations

Source: R/geometry3d.R
shape_mean.Rd

Two notions of mean shape for real landmark arrays: the full Procrustes mean, and the MDS (or \(\Phi\)) mean, an extrinsic mean obtained from the Veronese-Whitney embedding.

Usage

shape_mean(X, type = c("procrustes", "phi"), tol = 1e-12, max_iter = 1000L)

Arguments

X

Numeric array of dimension \(k \times m \times n\), with \(m\) equal to 2 or 3.

type

"procrustes" (default) or "phi".

tol, max_iter

Convergence tolerance (relative change of the objective) and iteration cap of the Procrustes iteration. Used for type = "procrustes" only: the "phi" mean has an explicit formula and needs the Procrustes mean only to choose between a shape and its mirror image, for which a looser fixed tolerance is used.

Value

A \(k \times m\) matrix: a centered configuration of unit size (Frobenius norm 1) representing the mean shape. A warning is given if the Procrustes iteration does not reach tol within max_iter steps.

Details

Procrustes. The full Procrustes mean minimizes \(\sum_i d_F^2(x_i, \mu)\). It is computed by the fixed-point iteration \(\mu \leftarrow \mathrm{normalize}(\sum_i \cos\rho_i \, z_i R_i)\), where \(R_i \in SO(m)\) aligns the pre-shape \(z_i\) to \(\mu\), started at the first configuration. Each step does not decrease \(\sum_i \cos^2\rho_i\). For \(m = 2\) it agrees with the dominant eigenvector of \(\sum_i z_i z_i^*\). It is the mean that shapes::procGPA() returns in $mshape, up to the looser convergence tolerance of that function.

phi. The MDS mean takes the \(m\) leading eigenvectors \(v_j\) (eigenvalues \(\lambda_j\)) of \(n^{-1}\sum_i z_i z_i^\top\), forms the pre-shape \([\sqrt{\lambda_1} v_1, \dots, \sqrt{\lambda_m} v_m] / \sqrt{\lambda_1 + \dots + \lambda_m}\) and lifts it with the transposed Helmert sub-matrix. This is shapes::MDSshape(x) with its defaults (alpha = 1, projalpha = 1/2). Because \(z z^\top\) does not change under a reflection of \(z\), the last axis is flipped if that brings the mean closer to the Procrustes mean, exactly as in shapes::MDSshape.

References

Kent, J. T. (1994). The complex Bingham distribution and shape analysis. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B, 56, 285–299. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1994.tb01978.x

Dryden, I. L. and Mardia, K. V. (2016). Statistical Shape Analysis, with Applications in R, 2nd ed. Wiley, chapters 6 and 7.

See also

shape_kmeans, which updates its centers with these means.

Examples

set.seed(2)
base <- matrix(rnorm(8 * 3), 8, 3)
X <- array(rep(base, 20), dim = c(8, 3, 20)) +
  array(rnorm(8 * 3 * 20, sd = 0.05), dim = c(8, 3, 20))
mu <- shape_mean(X)
nu <- shape_mean(X, type = "phi")
# Both means are close to the template
shape_distance(array(c(mu, nu, base), dim = c(8, 3, 3)))
#>              [,1]         [,2]       [,3]
#> [1,] 0.0000000000 0.0001997356 0.01004940
#> [2,] 0.0001997356 0.0000000000 0.01003735
#> [3,] 0.0100493984 0.0100373527 0.00000000
